exposure: Both parietal peritoneum and rectus abdominis muscle left open
closure of the parietal peritoneum and reapproximation of rectus muscle
closure types of the anterior abdominal wall layers in cesarean section (CS) surgery
Closure of parietal peritoneum and/or rectus abdominis muscle during cesarean section
cohort: 180 patients who underwent C-section for various reasons
finding: Closing the parietal peritoneum alone after C-section was associated with higher pain scores at 6 and 12 hours post-op, but rectus abdominis muscle reapproximation did not increase pain, and neither closure type affected bowel motility.
mod_finding: There was no difference in the timing of return of bowel motility between groups of women who had different abdominal layers closed after cesarean.
